prompt: Reference photos: the boy in the first reference photo is the OLDER BROTHER and the girl in the second is the LITTLE SISTER. CLOTHING: ignore the clothes in the reference photos completely — dress them in traditional Korean HANBOK as described here (jeogori jacket with a goreum ribbon tie, and chima skirt or baji trousers). Only the face and hair come from the photos. Keep their face shape, hairstyle, eyes, eyebrows and smile recognisable, but translate them fully into the flat layered paper-cut picture-book style described here (simple paper shapes, not a photo, not realistic). A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. This is one DRAMATIC COMIC ACTION PANEL filling the ENTIRE image edge to edge (full-bleed, no border): bold dynamic composition, big flat paper speed-line strips, kid-friendly and funny, never scary. Palette: bright clear DAYTIME — soft sky blue, cream, straw gold, bark brown, fresh green leaves (this picture is generated as a bright day scene and will be darkened to night afterwards; do NOT draw night, moon or stars). Cute, round, friendly Korean picture-book characters for 3-4 year olds: big round white paper eyes with dark pupils, small pink cheek circles, simple rounded shapes, never scary. Composition, left to right: on the LEFT, a round grey stone well in a sunny yard; the tiger leans over the well rim and peers DOWN into the water with a puzzled face, fooled by the siblings' reflection shining on the water. On the RIGHT, a tall tree trunk rises to the top of the picture; HIGH UP on a thick branch near the top right corner, the two siblings sit side by side, hands over their mouths, giggling and peeking down at the tiger. EXACTLY THREE CHARACTERS IN THE WHOLE PICTURE: one tiger at the well, one boy and one girl together on the high branch. The boy and the girl appear ONLY ONCE, ONLY up in the tree — the ground beside the well is EMPTY except for the tiger; no child stands on the ground, no child beside the well, no extra person anywhere. The tiger: a chubby persimmon-orange tiger made of flat paper pieces with dark-brown stripe pieces, cream muzzle and belly, big round eyes, pink cheeks, round ears — funny and clumsy, never scary, no fangs; THE TIGER MUST BE DRESSED in the MOTHER'S clothes (this is essential — the tiger is disguised as the mother): a soft pastel-pink hanbok jeogori jacket with a dark-rose goreum ribbon tie, squeezed over its round belly, and a charcoal-grey chima skirt; no headscarf. A bare, undressed tiger is WRONG. The older brother: a small Korean boy about 4 years old with a round face, soft full cheeks, straight shiny black hair cut in a neat bowl cut with blunt straight bangs across the forehead, small almond eyes, a big cheerful toothy grin, wearing a denim-blue jeogori with a tiny red heart patch and cream pants. The little sister: a small Korean girl about 3 years old with a round face, chubby pink cheeks, dark-brown hair in two short high pigtails with soft wispy bangs, bright curious almond eyes, a sweet shy smile, wearing a soft pink jeogori and a fluffy pale-pink tulle-like chima skirt.  Skin tones are natural soft light peach, NOT yellow or orange; the scene is a bright, cheerful day. No text anywhere. Full-bleed illustration, no lime green.
